comments.body:
DECISION (operator-approved, 2026-08-30): **Option 1 — edge fix via nginx `proxy_redirect` prefix-restore.**

Scope for this ticket:
- Add a per-location `proxy_redirect` to the `/review/` block that restores the `/review/` prefix on the app's self-referential absolute redirects (post-a61d the app emits `https://$host/<route>`, so the rule is `proxy_redirect https://$host/ https://$host/review/;`), coexisting with a61d's existing scheme rules and the restated `proxy_redirect default;`.
- Pin it with a structural test over the RENDERED nginx config (reuse a61d's `_render_nginx()` harness in `tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py`), asserting `/review/health/`-style redirects retain the `/review/` prefix AND that the existing prefix-STRIPPING request path is unchanged (`GET /review/health` still reaches the app as `/health`).
- Add a guard comment + a test that pins the review-bot's redirect surface as same-app-only, so the documented residual (a future off-`/review/` absolute redirect would be wrongly prefixed) is caught if it ever changes.

Rationale + evidence: the review-bot is a plain `uvicorn rebar.review_bot.app:app` FastAPI service with NO `--root-path`, NO `RedirectResponse`, and no cross-host redirects — its only absolute redirects are Starlette trailing-slash 307s to its own routes. So the broad same-host rewrite has no legitimate redirect to corrupt today, and `proxy_redirect`'s host-anchored match cannot touch a cross-host redirect. This directly fixes the observed `Location` symptom regardless of app internals and reuses a61d's per-location + structural-test pattern.

Rejected Option 2 (app-side `root_path`/APIRouter mount): known FastAPI/Starlette gotcha — `root_path` does not reliably prepend the prefix to `redirect_slashes` `Location` headers, so it may not fix the observed symptom without larger app changes; bigger blast radius + more verification.

Deploy note: the code lands through Gerrit now; LIVE VALIDATION (AC4) is satisfied by the SAME operator edge-deploy that clears a61d's AC5 (gated on 1d1b's detect-signal + operator apply). Do NOT deploy or touch the box; do not block on live validation.

Dispatching a background /rebar-debug agent under this scope.

comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body:
## RCA (Phase 1 — proven root cause)

**Mechanism (confirmed).** `location /review/` uses the prefix-STRIPPING form
`proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:${REVIEW_BOT_PORT}/;` (rebar.conf.template:104), so the review-bot
never sees `/review/`. The app is a plain `uvicorn rebar.review_bot.app:app` FastAPI service —
`FastAPI(title=…, summary=…, lifespan=…)` with **no `root_path`, no `redirect_slashes` override**
(src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:491), routes `/health` `/webhook` `/rerun`, **no `RedirectResponse`
anywhere** in `src/rebar/review_bot/`, and the Dockerfile CMD carries **no `--root-path`**
(infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot:171). Its only absolute redirects are Starlette's
`redirect_slashes` 307s to its own routes, built from the forwarded `Host`. Post-a61d
(`FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS='*'`) that Location is `https://$host/<route>` — correct scheme, **no
`/review/` prefix**. None of a61d's three rules match a `https://$host/...` Location (they match
`http://…` prefixes and the loopback default), so the prefix is simply lost, the Location matches
no review-bot route, falls through to `location /` → Gerrit → 404.

**Runtime proof (real nginx 1.27-alpine + stub upstream emitting the Starlette-style absolute
redirect).** Faithful copy of the current post-a61d `/review/` block vs. the same block plus the
single new rule:

    CURRENT:  GET /review/health/ (Host: example.test) -> 307 Location: https://example.test/health          <-- prefix LOST (repro)
    FIXED:    GET /review/health/ (Host: example.test) -> 307 Location: https://example.test/review/health   <-- prefix RESTORED
    BOTH:     GET /review/health  (Host: example.test) -> reaches app as /health                              <-- prefix-strip request path UNCHANGED
    FIXED, a61d regression check (stub emits http://): -> 307 Location: https://example.test/health          <-- scheme still upgraded to https

**Fix.** Add one rule to the `/review/` block, after a61d's scheme backstops (default stays first):
`proxy_redirect https://$host/ https://$host/review/;`. nginx applies the first matching
`proxy_redirect`; the new rule's `https://$host/` prefix overlaps none of the existing rules
(which match `http://…`), so it neither shadows nor is shadowed by them — a61d's scheme guarantee
and the prefix-stripping request path are both preserved. Confirmed on real nginx above.

**Legitimacy = defect.** Violates the design contract that `/review/<route>/` must resolve to the
review-bot route, not a Gerrit 404 (ticket AC; a61d's sibling fix on the same block). Restoration,
not creation — no new capability, no new dependency.

**Caller/dependency sweep.** The changed artifact is a response-header rewrite on one location
block; the only "callers" are HTTP clients following the `/review/` Location. No behavioral
dependency on the prefix-less Location exists (it 404s today). Request-URI handling for the app is
untouched (proven above).

**Defect attribution (caused_by).** `git blame -w -M -C` of rebar.conf.template:103-104 → commit
`6cd6f4e1f7c0` ("S2 (786b): deploy Gerrit + review-bot receiver behind nginx/TLS"), a
new-file-creation commit (no carrier to walk through). That commit introduced the `/review/`
location block AND its prefix-stripping `proxy_pass` together; the app's Starlette `redirect_slashes`
absolute-URL behaviour is default-framework behaviour present since the block's creation. The
prefix loss was therefore **latent from day one — never a regression**. → caused_by
**786b-190d-5e3a-4194** (smelly-pane-bolt), close-class **preexisting**. (Arguable as `plan_defect`
since 786b's edge-setup plan omitted the prefix-restore; `preexisting` is the precise match because
the behaviour was latent-from-creation, not broken by a later change.)

**Residual (bounded).** The rule is a broad same-host rewrite: were the app ever to emit an
absolute redirect to a genuine non-`/review/` target on the same host, it would be wrongly
prefixed. Bounded by a guard comment in the template + a test pinning the review-bot redirect
surface as same-app-only (no `RedirectResponse`, no `root_path`, no cross-host/off-`/review/`
absolute redirect), which turns RED if the app ever grows one.

**Live-validation AC (edge probe) is DEFERRED to the operator edge-deploy** that also clears
a61d's AC5 (gated on bug 1d1b + operator apply). Not deploying; not blocking on it.

## Final report — fix landed and merged

**Status:** Code fix MERGED via Gerrit change 2438; ticket closed `preexisting`,
caused_by `786b-190d-5e3a-4194`. Live-validation AC deferred to operator edge-deploy (see the
`[non-codebase]` disposition comment above); non-blocking.

**Root cause (proven).** `location /review/` proxies with a prefix-STRIPPING
`proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:${REVIEW_BOT_PORT}/;`, so the review-bot never sees `/review/`.
Its only absolute redirects are Starlette slash-307s to its own routes, built from the public
`Host` header — so post-a61d it emits `https://$host/<route>` with no `/review/` to strip, and
the prefix is lost (→ 404 on Gerrit fallthrough). Confirmed on real nginx 1.27-alpine + a stub
upstream: current block loses the prefix; block + the one new rule restores it; both leave the
prefix-stripping REQUEST path (`GET /review/health` → app `/health`) unchanged, and a61d's
http→https scheme guarantee intact.

**Fix (Option 1, edge-only).** One per-location rule appended to the `/review/` block AFTER
a61d's scheme backstops (`proxy_redirect default;` stays first):
`proxy_redirect https://$host/ https://$host/review/;`. nginx applies the first MATCHING
redirect; this rule's `https://$host/` LHS overlaps none of a61d's `http://…` rules, so ordering
is safe and both a61d's scheme guarantee and the prefix-stripping request path are preserved.
A guard comment documents the same-app-only precondition + the broad-rewrite residual. No app
change (Option 2 rejected per 2026-08-30 decision).

**RED→GREEN.** 4 structural tests over the RENDERED config (reuse a61d's `_render_nginx()`):
(1) redirect Location retains `/review/`; (2) request path stays prefix-stripping; (3) a61d
scheme + default-first ordering intact; (4) review-bot redirect surface pinned same-app-only.
The two behaviour tests were legitimately RED before the rule (held out from the fixer);
sandboxed mutation check: delete the rule → RED, misorder `default` → RED, restore → GREEN.

**Gates:** plan-review certified; LLM-Review +1; Verified +1; completion-verifier signed.

**Parity sweep.** `/review/` is the ONLY prefix-stripping surface where external prefix ≠ app
internal path. `/opcert/` (no trailing slash, prefix preserved, guard-gated fail-closed),
`/mcp` (external==internal), Gerrit `/` — none can emit a prefix-losing redirect. No sibling
tickets needed.

**Residual (bounded).** A future off-`/review/` same-host absolute redirect would be wrongly
prefixed by the broad rewrite; bounded by the guard comment + the same-app-only test (turns RED
if the app ever grows such a redirect).

compiled_state.description:
## Summary

Discovered while confirming the root cause of `enchanting-phantastic-weevil`
(a61d-adf9-3725-4847). Independent of that ticket's scheme-downgrade concern, and deliberately
left out of its scope.

`location /review/` proxies with a prefix-STRIPPING form
(`proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:${REVIEW_BOT_PORT}/;`, `infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template`), so the
review-bot app never sees the `/review/` prefix. When the app emits an ABSOLUTE redirect it builds
it from the public `Host` header, so the emitted path has no `/review/` prefix to strip — and the
prefix is simply lost.

## Observed (deployed edge, unauthenticated)

    GET https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/review/health/
      -> HTTP/2 307, location: http://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/health

The correct target is `…/review/health`. `…/health` matches no review-bot location, falls through
to `location /` -> Gerrit, and 404s. Same for `/review/webhook/` and `/review/rerun/`.

## Root cause (PROVEN — see RCA comment)

Post-a61d the app emits `https://$host/<route>` (correct scheme, no `/review/`). None of a61d's
three rules match a `https://$host/...` Location (they match `http://…` prefixes + the loopback
default), so the prefix is lost. Confirmed on real nginx (1.27-alpine) + a stub upstream emitting
the Starlette-style absolute redirect: current block loses the prefix, block + the one new rule
restores it, and both leave the prefix-stripping REQUEST path (`GET /review/health` -> app
`/health`) unchanged.

Review-bot redirect surface is same-app-only: `uvicorn rebar.review_bot.app:app`, plain
`FastAPI(...)` (no `root_path`, no `redirect_slashes`), no `RedirectResponse`, no `--root-path`,
routes `/health` `/webhook` `/rerun`. So the broad same-host rewrite has no legitimate off-`/review/`
redirect to corrupt today.

## Chosen approach (Option 1 — operator-approved, verified)

Edge fix only. Add ONE per-location rule to the `/review/` block, AFTER a61d's scheme backstops
(the restated `proxy_redirect default;` stays FIRST):

    proxy_redirect https://$host/ https://$host/review/;

nginx applies the first matching `proxy_redirect`; the new rule's `https://$host/` prefix overlaps
none of the existing rules (they match `http://…`), so it neither shadows nor is shadowed by them.
a61d's scheme guarantee (http->https) and the prefix-stripping request path are both preserved.
Option 2 (app-side `root_path`/APIRouter mount) is REJECTED (operator decision 2026-08-30).

## Implementation plan

1. `infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template`, `/review/` block: append the one `proxy_redirect
   https://$host/ https://$host/review/;` rule after the two a61d scheme rules; add a guard comment
   documenting the same-app-only precondition + the residual.
2. Confirm the RENDERED config still passes `nginx -t` in a throwaway `nginx:1.27-alpine` container.

## Test plan (`tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py`, reuse a61d's `_render_nginx()` / `_location_body()`)

- (1) `/review/` block restores the prefix: a `proxy_redirect https://$host/ https://$host/review/;`
  rule is present.
- (2) request path unchanged: `/review/` still `proxy_pass …/;` (prefix-stripping) — no accidental
  break of the app's `/health` mapping.
- (3) a61d scheme guarantee still holds on `/review/` (no regression of the http->https rules or the
  `default`-first ordering).
- (4) ordering: the prefix-restore rule appears AFTER `default` (default first).
- (5) residual guard: pin the review-bot redirect surface as same-app-only over
  `src/rebar/review_bot/` (no `RedirectResponse`, no `root_path`/`--root-path`), so a future
  off-`/review/` absolute redirect that the broad rewrite would mis-prefix is caught.

Structural tests run in-process (no CI provider dependency) — portable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] It is established which absolute URLs the review-bot app can emit (same-app-only; RCA comment).
- [x] A request to `https://<host>/review/<route>/` receives a `Location` retaining the `/review/`
      prefix, verified by a structural test over the rendered nginx config.
- [x] The existing prefix-stripping request behaviour is unchanged: `GET /review/health` still
      reaches the app as `GET /health`.
- [ ] [non-codebase] LIVE VALIDATION (DEFERRED to operator edge-deploy): an unauthenticated probe of
      `/review/health/` on the deployed edge shows a `Location` resolving to the health endpoint.
      Satisfied by the SAME operator edge-deploy that clears a61d's AC5 (gated on bug 1d1b +
      operator apply). Not deployed here; not blocking.
      provenance: environment=production-edge (rebar.solutions.navateam.com); principal=operator; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — deferred to the operator edge-deploy gated on bug 1d1b (downy-feminist-leopard) plus an operator apply; the same deploy clears a61d's AC5; not performed in this code-only change.

## Defect attribution

caused_by **786b-190d-5e3a-4194** (smelly-pane-bolt, "infra: S2 — deploy Gerrit + review-bot behind
nginx/TLS"); commit `6cd6f4e1f7c0` created the `/review/` block + prefix-stripping proxy_pass in one
new-file commit; the prefix loss was latent from creation -> close-class **preexisting**.

## Notes

Reported from unauthenticated probes and repo inspection only. No credential was transmitted.

Structural tests over the rendered nginx config: prefix-restore rule present, ordering (default first), request-path unchanged, a61d scheme guarantee intact, and a same-app-only redirect-surface guard over src/rebar/review_bot/.
